lenses.summary:
AI is already structural in this business: it writes master tours (A1), atomizes itineraries (A3), drafts and checks place cards, decides which DataForSEO keywords get bought, rewrites tours in each B2B tenant's voice (T2), writes social and blog pieces (T8/T9), judges and gates them (T10/F9), and narrates B2C trips in TripPlanner. Governance is ahead of most teams of this size. CIS has a DB-driven Model Gateway (llm_role_config, llm_model_catalog, Stage Routes with fallback and shadow), a CI test that blocks raw model calls, a vendor-separation rule (Anthropic writes, OpenAI judges, validate stages can use any vendor), the Jev decide() layer (a DB CHECK refuses enforce without a calibration record), per-job cost attribution and an External Spend page reconciled against Cost Explorer. The gaps sit at the edges, and they matter more as the stated direction becomes "AI-first for the whole ecosystem":
(1) The gateway is "single" only inside CIS. TripPlanner runs a 269-line fork that ignores shadow routes, logs only successful calls and is tagged only by JSON (quality_signal.app). Booking has no path at all yet.
(2) llm_call_log under-counts and under-describes. Rows are written by the caller and only on success, so attempts that failed a schema check after the model answered (billed tokens) are never logged. A lost row never raises: S223/S224 lost about $4.75 of Jev spend this way. The table has no app, shadow, status, latency or prompt_version columns, and the judge's median-of-3 repeats collapse into one row, so S235 needed an ad-hoc rerun to see brand_fit swing 4–8.
(3) AI decides more than it is evaluated. eval-regression covers only the A1 s1_old pipeline, runs on demand, pins Haiku and has no committed baseline. The T2 judge (brand_fit noise 4–8 on the same draft) and F9 (verdict agreement 0.87, 8 of 23 pieces non-unanimous) gate tenant-delivered content without a stability gate.
(4) Spend and data controls are uneven. The cost guard covers only segment_research and s1_seo_prefetch, against ADR 0001 decision 4, which says every LLM/Jev spend. TripPlanner's public narration endpoint has no rate limit or budget. Tenant T2 content goes to the OpenAI platform API (GPT-4.1 brand audit), while Jev is held behind a DPA allowlist.
(5) Jev questions are seeded shadow: 25 questions across 12 migrations, plus 3 more in 211/193/194. decision_log holds about 314k verdicts, yet the repo has no calibration-to-enforce pipeline, so paid verdicts mostly change nothing.
The recommended platform moves are listed below. Do the first three before scaling AI into Booking or prod: an AI Use Register with CI enforcement, llm_call_log v2 with attempt-level logging, and one shared gateway package for TP and Booking. Then come judge stability and eval harnesses, a Jev calibration workbench, a universal cost and egress policy at the gateway, and account-level Bedrock guardrails.

DECIDES vs ASSISTS - AI DECIDES with no human by default in these places: A3 atoms (a3_atomize feeds Segment/Score/Route and TripPlanner), auto_checked place cards fed to writers, the segment_research keyword loop (decides DataForSEO purchases, capped by cost guard), T2 judge retry/HITL (score <7, MIN_QUALITY graph.py:39; mission cap 6.0, judge_node.py:31-36), and T10 F9 block/hold. Per memory 'tenant-sees-content-only', T2/T9 content is always delivered to the tenant and gates surface only in admin. AI ASSISTS (a human or deterministic rule keeps final say) in these places: A1 brand audit fails closed to manual_check (CONTEXT.md:96-97), A2 HITL queue, T8 angles (tenant picks 1 of 3), Jev (all shadow, observe-only), admin sentence 'suggest' (t9_repair), and TripPlanner narration (deterministic grounding filter).

LOGGING - CIS: LLMClient.generate does not log; 'the caller writes the llm_call_log row' (CONTEXT.md:101-103). A CI guard blocks raw Bedrock/OpenAI calls, but it scans only services/, api/ and shared/ (tests/unit/test_aa685_no_raw_model_calls.py:12), so scripts/bedrock.py:164-174 and scripts/phaseb_rerun_sonnet.py:14-15 call models raw. record_call never raises and only logs a warning on failure (shared/llm_client/call_log.py:155,183,209). Lesson: a $11.8 Jev bill against $7.05 logged, with the gap equal to log_write_failed (skill/aa-lessons/lessons.md:13).

LOGGING - Failed route attempts are not costed: _call_route catches the exception and moves to the next model (shared/llm_client/client.py:139-145), including _checked_json schema failures raised after the model returned billed output (client.py:36-42,473,488,592). Luna drops brand-audit 'status' on about 15% of calls (CONTEXT.md:94-95), so those billed tokens are invisible.

LOGGING - Judge repeats are collapsed. score_brand_fit runs up to 3 calls (median) only when the first score falls in 6-8 (services/content_generation/brand_fit.py:36-42,256-260). A first score of 4-5 or 9 is accepted from a single noisy call. judge_node writes ONE llm_call_log row with summed cost and only the median score (judge_node.py:211-219). Per-repeat scores go only to structlog 'judge_repeat_median' (brand_fit.py:271).

LOGGING - TripPlanner: its own gateway fork writes llm_call_log only for successful calls, never raises on a log failure (backend/shared/llm_gateway.py:256-269), tags the app only inside JSON quality_signal.app='tripplanner' (llm_gateway.py:30,259), reads no shadow_model_id or shadow_sample_pct (llm_gateway.py:107-109), so an admin-set TP shadow is silently ignored, and prices a NULL catalog price as 0.0 (llm_gateway.py:124-125). There is no tenant, job or subject id.

LOGGING - Schema: shared.llm_call_log (about 244k rows) has no app, is_shadow, status/error, latency_ms, prompt_version or subject_key columns. Only content_piece_id and angle_gate_request_id are typed (db-schema-reference.md:852-871). Shadow rows are marked only by quality_signal {shadow:true} (shared/llm_client/shadow.py:55), and every consumer must remember to exclude them (migration 223:26-29,124 does). The S235 data lens flagged 'llm_call_log lacks app column ... shadow in same table; no cross-app spend view' (docs/audits/2026-10-14-S235-ecosystem-team-pilot/lenses/lens-data.md:12). prompt_version exists only for the S1 graph (services/content_generation/graph.py:234,403).

EVAL - eval-regression.yml is workflow_dispatch only, with options [s1_old] (apps/AA-CIS-App/.github/workflows/eval-regression.yml:13-20). It pins model_tier='haiku' (services/eval/regression.py:166), so it does not exercise the live stage route. The golden set (20 tours) lives only in S3 (regression.py:20-23,40-41). services/eval/baselines/ does not exist in the repo, although ITINERARY_BASELINE_PATH points there. No eval covers T2, T9/F9, place cards, atomize or tp_compose. S235 judge evidence came from ad-hoc scripts (t2-rerun/driver.py, aa786-f9-replay/aa786_replay.py).

JUDGE NOISE (S235) - The T2 brand_fit repeat noise is 4-8 on the same draft (00-orchestrator-journal.md:53,57-58). After the #708 fix, judge >= 7 on 6/9 and mission_present 19/50 (t2-rerun/summary.txt). F9 v1.1 3-run replay: mean verdict agreement 0.87 (15/23 unanimous), flagged-sentence Jaccard 0.676, with pieces flipping pass <-> block_quoted (aa786-f9-replay/aa786_replay.md:6-9). AA-801 (T2 judge stability) was created (journal:60).

COST CONTROL - ADR 0001 decision 4 says every external spend (DFS, LLM, Jev) checks a DB budget per run and per day (docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-target-architecture.md:44-46). In code, cost_guard is used only by segment_research, segment_research_batch, s1_seo_prefetch and the DFS client (grep: services/acp_contract/segment_research.py:54, services/jobs/s1_seo_prefetch_job.py:13). T2, T9, place cards, atomize, Jev and tp_compose have no budget gate. TripPlanner backend has no rate-limit or budget code, and tripplanner.tf has no throttling settings, although the public narration endpoint invokes Sonnet.

ACCOUNTS/INFRA - The acc3 invoker AA3-Bedrock-Invoker trusts both the CIS ECS task role and the TripPlanner Lambda role with the SAME ExternalId 'aa296-satellite-bedrock-acc3' (infra/AA-CIS-Infra/accounts/acc3-bedrock/main.tf:18-49), so AWS cost data cannot split CIS from TP Bedrock spend. There is one AWS Budget ($250/mo, acc2 only; accounts/aa365/observability.tf:239-253) and none on acc1/acc3. No Terraform for Bedrock model-invocation logging or Bedrock Guardrails was found. The blueprint notes all LLM egress goes through a single NAT t4g.nano with no alarm. acc1 AA-Bedrock-Invoker was created by hand outside IaC (project CLAUDE.md), with a later import file at accounts/acc1-bedrock/bedrock_invoker_import.tf.

STRENGTHS to keep - Model change audit (role_config._insert_audit, role_config.py:44). Jev enforce needs a calibration record (DB CHECK). Fail-closed brand audit. Cross-vendor writer/judge rule enforced at route save (ADR 0006/0008). Job-bound cost (call_log.bind_job/bind_tenant, call_log.py:41-89). External Spend vs Cost Explorer page. The lessons log captures AI-specific failure modes (lessons.md:12,13,22,33,36,56,57,62,79).

lenses.summary:
AA's customer-facing AI today is a careful but thin layer on a deterministic core. TripPlanner (the O8 front door) already does the hard, trustworthy part well. It builds trips only from real AA tour legs: the Tour Graph, coverage DP and route proposals use no model call. Narration prefers AA's own authored day text and drops LLM lines with invented numbers, and every model call goes through the CIS Model Gateway with a cost row. What is missing is the "AI-first" experience on top of it.

- **No conversational or intent layer.** Routes take only country + days. There is no taste-aware ranking or "why this fits".
- **Taste is per trip only.** The taste vector is just the average of the pins in the current trip, with no profile.
- **No multilingual surface.** The UI is hard-coded `lang="en"`, and CIS writers only handle en-US/en-GB even though DE/FR/NL are scored buyer markets.
- **No "from" prices yet.** The Booking view in ADR 0005 is still a plan.
- **No per-session cost or abuse controls.** There is no API GW throttling, no rate limit, no narration cache, and no session id on call-log rows.
- **Search has a quality bug.** Queries are embedded as `search_document` instead of `search_query`.
- **Read paths do not exclude stale or inactive tours.** Search, suggestions and routes have no active-tour filter, so the planner can still offer what AA no longer sells.

Recommended order:
1. Close the cheap correctness and guardrail gaps first: query embedding, active-tour filter, rate limits and session cost, a narration cache.
2. Add deterministic interest-aware routes with templated explanations, plus a structured intake that enriches inquiry.submitted.
3. Only then build a tool-calling trip designer whose model can act only through the existing grounded endpoints. It should be guarded by the writer-source-fidelity A/B policy: verified place-card facts allowed, tour promises forbidden. It also needs an eval set, because today eval-regression covers only `s1_old`.

Multilingual and "from" prices depend on ecosystem work: CIS translation as a content job (ADR 0002), the `catalog.tour.v1` views (AA-679), and the `booking.v_from_prices` / `price.from.v1` contract, which is not in the contracts registry yet.
current_state: The TripPlanner AI stack is three gateway stages. tp_compose is narration on Claude Sonnet 4.6 via the acc3→acc1 satellite. tp_search_embed is one Cohere Embed v4 call per free-text search on acc2. tp_extract / tp_component_embed run offline. All go through backend/shared/llm_gateway.py and write shared.llm_call_log tagged app=tripplanner (apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/CONTEXT.md:133-149).

Trip composition is deterministic and grounded in real tours. Route proposals are one leg or two chained legs of real AA tours for (country, days), ranked by whole-tour first, then duration fit, transfers and places (backend/browse/routes.py:1-12, 80-102). The coverage DP minimises gaps, transfers, moved pins and days, with no model call (backend/assembly/coverage.py:1-17). This implements ADR 0001 decision 5 (docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-target-architecture.md, decision 5).

Route proposals take only country + days (routes.py:126-128, SQL $1 country / $2 days). There is no activity, intensity, season, budget or free-text intent input, and the response carries ranking facts (whole_tour, transfers, transfer_km) but no human-readable reason (routes.py:141-148).

Narration grounding has three layers. Authored AA day prose comes first, at no model cost (backend/assembly/master_content.py:1-18). The LLM fills only missing days (handler.py:296-315). LLM lines stating a number absent from the component texts are replaced (backend/assembly/grounding.py:39-66). Grounding is numeric only: it explicitly 'does not judge qualitative claims' (grounding.py:6-7), so B-class promises about activities, services or views are covered only by the prompt (backend/assembly/agent.py:22-35).

The writer-source-fidelity policy (S223, AA-756) allows short well-known background about a named place (A) and forbids any unstated claim about the tour (B: activities, food, services, transport, times, views, inclusions) (memory writer-source-fidelity-policy.md:11-15).

Semantic search embeds the user query with input_type="search_document" (backend/browse/search.py:77). The project's own note says queries should use "search_query" (backend/extraction/backfill_embeddings.py:19). Cohere Embed v4 is asymmetric, so query ranking is degraded. Search has no query-embedding cache ('NOT cached', search.py:5) and no query length cap in browse/handler.py.

The search SQL ranks itinerary_components by cosine distance with no active/published-tour filter (search.py:46-57). The AA-731 'orphans' op only reports inactive-tour rows (backend/extraction/lambda_entry.py:12, 89-91; tour_days.py:360). itinerary_components is not refreshed automatically after CIS reruns (CONTEXT.md:171-173).

Personalization: the taste vector is the average embedding of the components pinned in the current trip, blended 0.6 taste + 0.4 geography, with route-constrained candidates (backend/assembly/suggestions.py:13-15, 49-60, 69-100). No taste or preference profile is stored. The schema has customers/sessions/trip_events/trip_drafts and no preference columns (migrations/001_tripplanner_schema.sql:66-120).

Multilingual: TripPlanner has no i18n library (frontend/package.json:12-17) and renders <html lang="en"> (frontend/app/layout.tsx:23). CIS stores rewrite_language but the writer prompt only distinguishes en-GB from American English (apps/AA-CIS-App/services/content_generation/batch_prompt.py:152-160). DE/FR/NL exist only as SEO and ranking buyer markets (AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:401, 784-785).

Prices: ADR 0005 defines the 'from' price as the lowest per-person B2C price for 2 pax in low season, exposed as booking.v_from_prices / contract price.from.v1. TripPlanner never computes prices (docs/adr/0005-pricing-and-supplier-rates.md:46-60). AA-Booking has only the health slice and bk-001 (.tmp-session/wt/aa-booking/CONTEXT.md:1-8, 108-116). price.from.v1 is missing from the contracts registry (docs/contracts/README.md:30-37).

Abuse and cost controls: the TripPlanner API GW stage has no throttling settings (infra/AA-CIS-Infra/accounts/aa365/tripplanner.tf:435-445). The only gate is a shared BFF secret (backend/shared/auth.py:1-13). The narrate endpoint requires session_id but loads the itinerary by trip_id alone (handler.py:165-185). Each click is a fresh Sonnet call with no cache. llm_call_log quality_signal carries mode/source/days but no session_id or trip_id (handler.py:187-192), so cost per session cannot be computed. shared.spend_budget is used only by CIS (apps/AA-CIS-App/shared/cost_guard.py:3, 162). TripPlanner has no budget check (grep returns nothing).

Accessibility and analytics: MapView.tsx (752 lines) and Header.tsx have 0 aria/role attributes; planning is map-first. There is no analytics or funnel instrumentation in the frontend (no analytics deps or imports).

CIS has grounded content assets TripPlanner could use but does not read. acp_shared.place_card holds ~102 cards with identity plus 4-6 facts kept only when a second vendor marks them 'supported'; trip facts (prices, hours, what the tour does) are never card facts (apps/AA-CIS-App/services/acp_shared/place_cards.py:1-38; docs/architecture/db-schema-reference.md:439-475). acp_contract.atom_embedding has ~6,744 rows (db-schema-reference.md:37-43). Jev decide() offers calibrated questions such as a1_claim_supported with off/shadow/enforce modes (AA-CIS-App/CONTEXT.md:121-133, 588-620). The blueprint (01-ecosystem-blueprint.html, 'Hành trình khách mục tiêu') wants CIS content and tenant pages to deep-link into TripPlanner. Today CIS publishes only to tenant WordPress (lenses/lens-tripplanner.md:2).

The hand-off to humans is thin. Advisor notification is a stub that emails a raw event log (backend/assembly/notify.py:34-50). inquiry.submitted v1.1 carries customer + leg chain + days + custom_days (docs/contracts/inquiry.submitted.v1.1.json) but no pax, dates, budget, locale or interests (lens-tripplanner.md:8). Registration links sessions to existing customers by an unverified phone/email match (backend/assembly/registration.py:19-26), flagged High in the blueprint.

The eval harness is the eval-regression workflow: workflow_dispatch only, pipeline options [s1_old] only (apps/AA-CIS-App/.github/workflows/eval-regression.yml:1-24). No customer-facing narration or recommendation is under regression eval.

lenses.summary:
Verdict on the main question: yes, make the CIS Model Gateway a shared platform service. Ship it as a versioned in-process Python library that all apps call, backed by the existing shared control plane in the acc2 RDS (shared.llm_model_catalog, llm_role_config, spend_budget, llm_call_log, decision_question/decision_log), with CIS owning that control plane. Do not build an internal HTTP API now.

Why a library: all three apps (CIS, TripPlanner, Booking) are Python on acc2 and share one RDS. ADR 0003 §4 already chose "shared library, forced on none" for jobs and names shared/llm_client as the model, and Booking O3 (14/10) adopted the same pattern. An internal API would put the CIS ECS service on TripPlanner's synchronous public path (tp_compose). It would also need service-to-service auth, which does not exist today (lens-infra).

ADR 0005 §9's trigger ("move the gateway when a second app needs it") has already fired. TripPlanner runs a 269-line fork (backend/shared/llm_gateway.py) that has drifted from the CIS gateway (3,561 lines). The fork has no OpenAI provider, no shadow, no output-schema check, no cost guard, logs successful calls only, and falls back to a hardcoded Sonnet 4.6 route when it cannot read the DB tables. Booking is about to become the third consumer.

Revisit an internal API only if one of these happens: a non-Python consumer appears, the OpenAI/TypeSafe keys must leave the app task roles, tenant quotas need atomic cross-process counters, or prod isolation requires it.

Beyond packaging, these gaps stand between today and "AI-first for the whole ecosystem":
1. **Spend is visible but not capped.** The cost guard covers only segment_research and s1_seo_prefetch. Tenant LLM cost shows in v_tenant_monthly_usage but nothing enforces it. Public TripPlanner assembly calls Sonnet with no budget.
2. **Evals are manual and partly off-platform.** The only eval workflow (eval-regression.yml) is manual and covers s1_old only. The golden set is a 20-tour xlsx in S3. Human labels (AA-783) live in an xlsx. The S234 judging panel ran as local Claude Code agents, not through the gateway.
3. **Judges are noisy.** The T2 brand_fit judge scored the same draft anywhere from 4 to 8. The Luna models ignore temperature/seed, and the AA-346 lesson shows run-to-run noise can exceed the effect of a prompt change.
4. **Prompts are versioned only in S1.** prompt_version (a hash) exists only on S1; T-series and TripPlanner prompts are inline constants.
5. **The data-governance rule is uneven.** Jev (TypeSafe) gets tenant content only for allow-listed tenants until a DPA is in place. But the default T2/T10 judge fallback chain includes the OpenAI API with no equivalent check, and Booking will soon handle customer PII.
6. **The call log cannot split spend by app or show failures.** It has no app column, no latency or prompt version, and no rows for failed calls.
7. **Satellite accounts are under-hardened.** CIS and TripPlanner share one ExternalId on acc3. Bedrock invocation logging and budgets are not in Terraform for acc1/acc3. The model IAM allow-list is edited separately from the catalog.

The 14 opportunities below are ordered so that platform foundations (library, logging, budgets, governance) come before new AI features for Booking and TripPlanner.
current_state: The single Model Gateway is decided at ecosystem level. Root ADR 0001 decision 2 (docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-target-architecture.md:37-48) says every LLM, Jev and embedding call goes through one gateway: DB catalog, stage routing with fallback and shadow, seams generate/decide/embed, Bedrock Converse, and a cost log for every call. New models run on acc3 only.

CIS gateway = apps/AA-CIS-App/shared/llm_client/ (16 files, 3,561 lines: client.py 608, decide.py 704, role_config.py 348, catalog.py 266, call_log.py 209, schema_check.py 58, shadow.py 65, prompt_cache.py 55, embed.py 155, bedrock_satellite.py 362, bedrock_batch.py 295).

ADR 0005 §9 (apps/AA-CIS-App/docs/adr/0005-model-catalog-and-converse-adapter.md) says the catalog is CIS-owned and the gateway code stays in CIS 'until a second app actually needs it (P5)'. TripPlanner already needs it (CIS CONTEXT.md:274-275; migration 173 grants).

TripPlanner runs a forked gateway, apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/backend/shared/llm_gateway.py (269 lines). It reads role_config/catalog (:100-136) and supports only anthropic_native and converse on Bedrock (:170-195): no OpenAI API path, no shadow, no JSON-schema check, no cost guard. It writes llm_call_log only for successful calls (:256-269) and tags the app in quality_signal.app. Its builtin fallback route is hardcoded Sonnet 4.6 for tp_compose/tp_extract (:75-81).

Stage routes (ADR 0006): model_id + ordered fallback_model_ids + shadow_model_id/shadow_sample_pct live in shared.llm_role_config. On total failure the call raises, naming every attempt (client.py:129-151). Shadow runs on a daemon thread and is lost on deploy (client.py:153-187; ADR 0006 consequences). SAFE_DEFAULTS cover about 30 stages (role_config.py:70-134).

Vendor rule: writers are Anthropic, judges are non-Anthropic, validate stages may use any vendor (ADR 0008). Default judge route = GPT-5.6 Luna (acc3) → ('gpt-6-luna', 'gpt-6-luna-openai', 'gpt-4.1') (role_config.py:70, :88-106). The last two run on the OpenAI platform API with a separate key (infra accounts/aa365/variables.tf:106).

Structured output: the CIS gateway checks every structured response against its schema and moves the route on when it does not match (schema_check.py:1-10; ADR 0006 §6). Luna left a required key out on the first live run and drops 'status' on about 15% of brand audits (CIS CONTEXT.md:94-96).
Raw-call guard: tests/unit/test_aa685_no_raw_model_calls.py fails on any invoke_model/converse outside shared/llm_client, and its ALLOWED list is empty since AA-757. Guard scope: CIS repo only.

llm_call_log (about 244k rows) has columns tenant_id, stage, role, model, tokens, cost_usd, quality_signal, stop_reason, account, fallback_used, provider, job_id. It has no app, latency, prompt_version or error/status column (docs/architecture/db-schema-reference.md:852-871). The caller writes the row, not the gateway (CIS CONTEXT.md:101-103). llm_shadow_log (about 5.5k rows) stores full primary and shadow outputs plus request_sha256, with no tenant/job/prompt version (schema ref :912-926). The AA-686 agreement_rate was once always null for s1_judge (lessons.md:36).

GPT-4.1 had scored every tour 9 (CIS CONTEXT.md:93).

Per-domain caches are bespoke: debate_brand_fit_cache, place_card + place_card_miss (AA-772), Jev verdict cache, DFS 7-day cache. There is no generic response cache. lenses.summary:
Adventure Asia already runs a real AI-first engineering loop. One person (Nghiệp) acts as approver. A Claude Code orchestrator plans the work, implementer lanes and reviewer agents do it, and Kiro is used for well-scoped backend tasks. Guardrail hooks stop subagents from releasing anything, and a serial merge train gates merges and deploys behind "Done = live-verified" (aa-ship). Output is high. must_have_guardrails: Numbers come only from deterministic code. No LLM output may set, alter or restate a price, margin, FX rate, net rate, date or pax count that is then stored or sent. Any number in AI text must match an allowed set via the grounding.py pattern, or the text is replaced. This applies to TripPlanner narration, Booking drafts and tenant content alike (ADR 0005 is deterministic pricing; grounding.py:28-36 allowed-set mechanism).

Every AI output that reaches a customer or tenant passes a check that blocks or removes fabricated claims before delivery, not only a flag shown in admin. Today T2/T9 'held' content is delivered and can be published by tenants (CIS CONTEXT.md:530-532; memory tenant-sees-content-only). That rule is compatible with a deterministic auto-cut of F9 block_quoted / B-class sentences before delivery. Nghiệp must rule on this before the first real paying tenant, because the current tenants (Atlas, Terra, Trail, WildKind; journal:51) are test tenants.

Data-class egress rule enforced in the gateway. Tenant content and customer PII never go to a provider without a recorded DPA/ZDR: the OpenAI platform API (gpt-4.1, gpt-6-luna-openai) and TypeSafe. The gateway skips those route entries instead of relying on a convention. This matters now because s1_brand_audit's primary is GPT-4.1 on the OpenAI API and t2_brand_audit copied that route (CONTEXT.md:94-97; migration 219:15,25-31), while the judge fallbacks also end on OpenAI-API models (role_config.py:70,88-106). First run one read-only query: llm_call_log WHERE provider='openai' AND tenant_id IS NOT NULL.

Hard spend caps on every paid path, with a stop rather than only an alert, for any endpoint reachable from the public internet. tp_compose/narrate gets API GW throttling plus a per-day spend_budget check plus a session-owns-trip check (handler.py:165-185 loads by trip_id only). Every batch job kind gets a per-run cap, as ADR 0001 decision 4 says (adr/0001:44-46), which today holds only for segment_research, s1_seo_prefetch and DFS.

Every billed model attempt is logged, including schema-failed and errored attempts, by the gateway rather than the caller. A log-write failure must page someone, not only print a warning. Today client.py:139-145 swallows failed attempts after billed output, TripPlanner's llm_gateway.py:256-269 logs successes only and prints on failure, and S223 lost $4.75 of Jev rows (lessons.md:13). Reconcile monthly against the provider dashboard before any cost number is reported.

Untrusted-text rule for prompt injection. Text from suppliers, customers, tenant websites, SERP/PAA results and crawled pages is data only. Stages that read it output a strict JSON schema, have no tools that send, spend, publish or change state, and every action they propose needs a human click. Loops that can spend money (the segment_research ReAct loop chooses paid DFS calls from SERP text, segment_research.py:91-116) keep hard per-run caps (MAX_SERPS=2) so a successful injection is cheap. prompt_sanitize.py:12-14 is explicitly only self-injection containment and must not be cited as a defence.

No AI auto-sends anything to a customer, tenant or supplier, and AI never counts as the checker in maker-checker. Booking AI is draft-only and a named human sends. ADR 0005 maker-checker needs two named people. If only Ms. Thư holds the contracting role, publishing rates waits for the second person; it does not fall back to the AI.

No enforce mode without a calibration record built from human labels, and no paid question or shadow without an end date. This is the Jev DB CHECK (181:38-40) generalised. Any judge or Jev question that gates content needs measured test-retest stability on a fixed set. T2 brand_fit swung 4–8 on the same draft (journal:53) and F9 verdict agreement was 0.87 (aa786_replay.md:6-9), so neither may trigger more than a retry or an admin label until it is stable. Shadow questions with no promotion plan are switched off.

Every PR that changes a writer or judge prompt, a route or a model has evidence attached. Prompt bytes are pinned by hash in CI (generalise test_aa792_a1_prompt_golden.py), and a capped replay on the committed golden set uses the A/A' rule: a delta counts only if it exceeds the repeat spread (lessons.md:63,71). Paid runs follow trial-3 then ≤50.

Kill switch and degraded mode per app and per stage. An admin can set any stage to off or deterministic fallback without a deploy. TripPlanner falls back to AA-authored day text, CIS jobs pause, and Booking works with no AI at all. Writers are Anthropic-only by vendor rule, and Converse-only models have no cross-account fallback, so an acc3 outage or quota cut must degrade gracefully, not fail customer flows.

No passport, payment or full rooming data goes into prompts. llm_call_log.quality_signal and llm_shadow_log, which stores full primary and shadow outputs (schema ref :912-926), must never hold raw customer PII. Shadow outputs need a retention limit and a deletion path before Booking or TripPlanner customer text touches the gateway (GDPR exposure for EU B2C markets).

Agent guardrails are fail-closed and tested. The subagent hook must parse argv instead of matching substrings. Today 'git -C <dir> push', 'aws --profile X ecs update-service' and 'gh api -XPOST' pass (subagent-guardrails.sh:12-24). A committed bypass test table backs the parser. Vendor lock-in and exit plans. Writers are Anthropic-only by rule. Judges depend on fictional-tier 'Luna' models that ignore temperature and seed. Then the gateway skips OpenAI-API and TypeSafe route entries for tenant or customer data unless a DPA/ZDR is recorded, mirroring jev_tenant_allowlist (decide.py:192-239). 5. llm_call_log minimum v2 (S, one CIS migration plus a gateway change). The gateway, not the caller, writes a row per attempt, including schema_fail and error attempts with their billed tokens. Add typed app, is_shadow and status columns, and log judge repeats as separate rows. Leave latency_ms, subject_key and prompt_version until a consumer needs them. Alarm on *_log_write_failed instead of only warning.

6. Judge stability, minimal version (S–M, overlaps AA-801). Always take the median of 3 for T2 brand_fit. Today the median runs only when the first score is 6–8 (brand_fit.py:36-42), so a noisy single 4–5 or 9 decides. The extra cost is small against $0.27 per version. Commit the S235 T2 pairs and the 23 F9 pieces with t2-rerun/aa786_replay to git as capped suites, and require a run on any judge prompt or route change. A judge gates only a retry or an admin label until test-retest SD ≤ 1.

7. Prompt-bytes manifest CI gate (S). Generalise test_aa792_a1_prompt_golden.py to every stage in llm_role_config, including the T-series and tp_compose, so a shared-builder edit cannot silently change another stage (gate05 risk R2). A manifest change requires the item-6 replay evidence in the PR.

8. Agent guardrail hook rewrite (S). Argv/shlex parsing instead of substring grep, a committed bypass test table (git -C … push, aws --profile … ecs update-service, gh api -XPOST, bash -c wrappers), and removal of 'git push *' / 'terraform apply *' allowlist entries from the sub-repo settings.local.json. With one engineer and many agents, this is the highest-leverage safety item for development work.

9. TripPlanner cheap correctness, not new AI (S). Embed queries with input_type='search_query' (search.py:77 vs backfill_embeddings.py:19) and measure on a 30-query labelled set. Add an active-tour filter on search, suggestions and routes so the planner never offers tours AA no longer sells (search.py:46-57; ADR 0001 decision 5). Add funnel events so later AI-first claims can be measured.

10. Booking deterministic-first, with the gateway package timeboxed and triggered only by the first Booking AI slice. Add the inquiry.submitted v1.2 form fields (dates, pax, budget band, language, message), the ADR 0005 pricing engine and a deterministic quote margin/FX/expiry guard, with zero LLM. Freeze the TripPlanner gateway fork and patch its three concrete defects in the meantime: shadow ignored, success-only logging, NULL price→0. Extract aa_llm as a shared package only when a Booking AI feature, e.g. a draft-only consultant inquiry summary, is actually scheduled and items 2, 4 and 5 are done.

kill_or_defer.why: Blocked on bk-00x pricing migrations, price.from.v1 (not in the contracts registry), AA-679 catalog views and tenant resale terms (ADR 0005 decision 9). Nothing AI-specific should start before those exist.

must_have_guardrails: NUMBERS ARE NEVER MODEL OUTPUT. Prices, margins, FX, tax, availability, pax bands and dates come only from deterministic engines or structured data. Every number in any AI text (proposal, narration, translation, brief) must match an allowed set, as in grounding.py, or the text fails closed. Tax is not shown until tax_rules exists (ADR 0005 decision 10).

NO AI OUTPUT REACHES A CUSTOMER OR SUPPLIER WITHOUT A NAMED HUMAN ACTION. A person sends, publishes, sets is_sent_to_customer, confirms bookings, and marks payments verified. The AI is never counted as the checker in maker-checker. Tenant-delivered T2/T9 keeps its gates and the A4 force-unpublish net (admin_a4.py), plus the Trust Ramp.

ONE GATEWAY, GATEWAY-WRITTEN LEDGER. Every LLM, Jev or embedding call in every repo goes through the shared package, with a raw-call CI guard in CIS, TripPlanner and Booking, and scripts/ included (test_aa685 scans only services/api/shared today). The gateway itself writes one row per attempt, including schema-fail and error attempts, with app NOT NULL. A failed log write alarms and counts as an incident, not a warning.

DATA-CLASS EGRESS POLICY. Tenant content and customer PII go only to providers with a recorded DPA/ZDR (Bedrock acc3 yes; the OpenAI platform API and TypeSafe only for allow-listed tenants). The route is skipped otherwise. Passport, payment and rooming documents never go to an LLM. Deterministic PII redaction runs before egress. Retention limits apply to llm_shadow_log full outputs and quality_signal.

CHANGE MANAGEMENT FOR ROUTES, PROMPTS AND JUDGES. A model route, prompt or rubric change on a tenant- or customer-facing stage needs an eval run on the stage's committed golden set, with an A/A' noise band and a cost cap, linked from the PR or the audit row. Today an admin route save goes live in 20 s (role_config.py:29) on acc2, which ADR 0001:78 also names as future prod. One-click revert to the previous route is required.

HARD BUDGETS AT THE GATEWAY per app × stage × tenant × day, plus API GW throttling and a per-session cap on public TripPlanner endpoints, plus AWS Budgets and anomaly detection on acc1 and acc3. ADR 0001 decision 4 already says this; code covers only segment_research and s1_seo_prefetch.

THIRD-PARTY TEXT IS DATA, NOT INSTRUCTIONS. This covers supplier PDFs and emails, customer messages and tenant brand fields. Extraction stages return a strict schema only, with no tools. Document text never selects an action, recipient or price, and every extracted value must be quoted verbatim from the source.

REGULATED AND SAFETY CLAIMS ONLY FROM CURATED FACTS. Visa, health and altitude, safety, inclusions, prices and animal-welfare statements come only from the Facts Entry (platform scope, CIS CONTEXT.md:365) or structured data, never from model knowledge. The writer-source-fidelity A/B rule applies to all customer and tenant text. The elephant-riding policy means human review, never strip or regenerate. No fabricated testimonials or reviews, and no AI-generated destination imagery.

NO ENFORCE WITHOUT CALIBRATION. Any automated decision (Jev, judge gates, lead scores, anomaly blocks) runs in shadow until a calibration record exists from human labels (≥95% precision per ADR 0007), and grey or error results keep the existing rule. Every shadow has an expiry date and a decision owner.

KILL SWITCH AND RECALL. Each stage can be paused from admin without a deploy. Every AI-produced content row carries provenance (stage, model, prompt_hash, run/job id), so content made by a bad model, prompt or window can be listed and bulk-held or unpublished.

AI TRANSPARENCY. B2C narration and any chat are labelled as AI-assisted. Tenants receive a subprocessor/model-provider list and a statement of which checks their content passed. Check EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency duties with counsel, since DE/FR/NL buyers and tenants are in scope.

AGENT GUARDRAILS ARE PARSED, TESTED AND SHIPPED TO EVERY REPO. Today the substring hook lets `git -C … push`, `aws --profile X ecs update-service` and `gh api -XPOST` through, and settings.local.json allowlists `git push *` and `terraform apply *`. Merges, deploys, applies and MCP writes stay with the orchestrator or Nghiệp.
missing: DATA QUALITY IS THE REAL AI BOTTLENECK, AND NO LENS OWNS IT. lessons.md:61 says regeneration cannot fix poor raw input or a writer tone problem (AA-724). AA-690 found 6 of 12 supplier files silently dropping fields (column_mapper.py). 751 tours sit at pipeline_status='ingested' (CIS CONTEXT.md:668-672). There is no countries/ISO table, and places are duplicated across destinations, place_card, hub and TripPlanner tour_stop/graph (lens-data.md:9). Missing pieces: (a) a deterministic source-completeness score per raw tour, checked before A1/A3 spend (days, inclusions, group_size, best_time, photos, price_raw), that routes thin tours to a human enrichment queue instead of the writer; (b) one place/entity master with IDs shared by CIS, TripPlanner and Booking (supplier service ↔ place); (c) data-quality SLOs on the dashboard. Every AI stage downstream inherits this ceiling.

EVALUATION OWNERSHIP AND A HUMAN LABELLING LOOP ARE NOT DEFINED. No stage has a named quality owner or sign-off rule. It is unclear whether chị Thư owns brand_fit, F9 truth and place cards, and whether Nghiệp owns routes. Labels live in an xlsx (S234-label-40.xlsx, AA-783 still open) and decision_question.calibration_ref is free text. Missing: (a) a RACI per stage; (b) a labels table with labeller, rubric version and inter-rater agreement; (c) a weekly labelling budget, for example 30 minutes a week per reviewer, sized to how many enforce decisions it unlocks; (d) holdout discipline, so prompts are not tuned on the same golden items used to accept them; (e) golden-set refresh when the catalog or tenant mix changes.

FREE IMPLICIT LABELS ARE IGNORED. gold_aa_internal.tenant_tour_versions.edit_source distinguishes ai_generated from tenant edits (t2_rewrite_job.py:208; v1_tours.py:295,451). Tenants pick 1 of 3 angles (AngleGateWizard.tsx:19,95). Admins verify or reject place cards and resolve held pieces. None of these feed judge calibration or prompt evals. Capturing tenant edit diffs and rejections is the cheapest source of brand_fit ground truth, and it bears directly on AA-801.

THERE IS NO OUTCOME LEARNING LOOP FROM THE MARKET BACK TO CONTENT. Nothing ingests post-publish performance: there is no Search Console, GA or social metrics code in services/api (grep). Booking outcomes do not flow back either: inquiry.submitted legs carry source_tour_id, but nothing attributes inquiries or wins to tours, tenant pieces, angles or keywords. As a result, T8 angle ranking, segment_research keyword purchases (paid DataForSEO) and the judge's brand_fit are never validated against real demand. Needed: a content→inquiry→booking attribution model and a quarterly review of which AI decisions predicted outcomes.

MODEL AND ROUTE CHANGE MANAGEMENT IS NOT DEFINED. Route edits are audited (role_config._insert_audit) but go live within the 20 s cache (role_config.py:29), with no eval gate, canary percentage or staged rollout. Shadow is comparison only, not canary. There is no separate prod: ADR 0001:78 says prod also runs on acc2. llm_model_catalog has enabled/blocked_reason but no EOL or deprecation date (catalog.py:52,91), so a Bedrock model retirement or a price change appears only as fallback noise. Missing: a change-request record per route change (reason, eval run, rollback route), deprecation tracking, and a vendor-outage plan for Anthropic-only writer stages on acc3.

AI INCIDENT RESPONSE IS NOT DEFINED. There are no severity levels for AI failures: tenant receives a false claim, PII is egressed, a spend runaway, a judge outage that passes everything, a provider outage. There is no per-stage pause switch (no kill-switch code found). There is no bulk recall: force-unpublish is per item (admin_a4.py:24-28), and content rows lack model/prompt provenance, so 'everything T2 wrote with route X on day Y' cannot be listed. There is no tenant notification template and no postmortem habit beyond lessons.md. SNS alerts are email only (observability.tf:54-58).

TENANT-FACING AI TRANSPARENCY AND CONTRACT TERMS ARE MISSING. The 'tenant sees content only' rule hides gates, which is right for the UI, but tenants publish AI text under their own brand with no disclosure of which providers processed their brand pack. T2 brand audit runs on the OpenAI platform API (CIS CONTEXT.md:94-100; mig 219), and there is no subprocessor list. Also unclear: who carries liability for a false claim, what the takedown SLA is, and whether tenants can opt out of a vendor. EU AI Act Art. 50 (AI-interaction and published-text transparency) needs a legal check for DE/FR/NL-facing tenants and the B2C TripPlanner narration and chat.

MULTILINGUAL QA BEYOND TRANSLATION. Judges, F-gates, forbidden-word lists and grounding are calibrated on English only. The writer handles only en-US/en-GB (batch_prompt.py:152-160). Missing: (a) a per-language judge calibration set; (b) a transliteration/place-name glossary (Bhutanese, Mongolian, Lao names), tied to the place master; (c) a back-translation or number/date-drift check; (d) a native reviewer pool per market; (e) the Vietnamese/Thai supplier-language side for ops communications.

ACCESSIBILITY OF GENERATED CONTENT, NOT ONLY THE PLANNER UI. Nothing covers alt text for images in tenant WordPress and social pieces (a natural AI task with human spot-checks), reading level, or the accuracy of accessibility facts for travellers (mobility, altitude, walking load) as structured Facts rather than model prose. Customer intake needs mobility and dietary fields that feed AI drafting safely.

CONTENT FRESHNESS AND LINEAGE. When a raw tour, supplier rate, place card or Facts Entry changes, nothing marks downstream AI artifacts stale: atoms, embeddings, T2 rewrites, published tenant pieces, TripPlanner components (TP CONTEXT.md:171-173 covers only the TP index). An AI-first ecosystem needs a dependency graph (source → derived artifact with hashes) and regeneration or hold triggers. Lens-data.md:12 notes there is no lineage.

HUMAN REVIEW CAPACITY PLANNING. Every 'assist-only' proposal adds a queue: A2 HITL, held pieces, place-card verify, Jev labels, rate maker and checker, inquiry drafts, translation spot-checks, flag dismissals. All of them land on Nghiệp, chị Thư and an unnamed contracting person. There are no queue SLAs and no load model, and the lenses do not count reviewer-hours per proposal. AI-first can make the human the outage. Each feature needs a 'review minutes per week' estimate and a queue-age alarm.

ENVIRONMENT AND TENANT ISOLATION FOR EXPERIMENTS. Evals, shadow runs, ad-hoc replays (1,236 .tmp-session scripts) and real tenant-serving traffic share one acc2 DB and the same accounts. There is no 'is_test_tenant / experiment' flag on llm_call_log or content rows. Cost, quality metrics and tenant usage (mig 223 v_tenant_monthly_usage) can mix experiment and production spend.

SCALED-CONTENT AND SEO RISK ACROSS TENANTS. Many tenants publish rewrites of the same master tours. Cross-tenant similarity exists at write time (piece_similarity.py cross_tenant, AA-484 threshold), but nobody monitors indexing or ranking after publish, and there is no policy for search-engine scaled-content rules. A penalty would hit tenants first. Needed: a published-piece index or coverage monitor per tenant and a quarterly duplicate audit.

IP AND RIGHTS. Supplier source text is rewritten and redistributed to B2B tenants, and photos come from GDrive (aa-cis/dev/gdrive-photo-reader). No lens checks usage rights for supplier itineraries and photos in tenant republication, or bans AI-generated destination imagery that would misrepresent a trip (package-travel misrepresentation risk).

UNIT ECONOMICS PER BUSINESS OBJECT. Spend is tracked by stage and tenant, but not as cost per published master tour, per tenant piece, per inquiry or per confirmed booking against revenue or margin. There is no ROI target for each AI stage, so 'AI-first' has no stop rule. Agent dev spend is also unmeasured (engineering lens).

CONSISTENCY ACROSS LENSES. The lenses propose an AI Use Register, ledger v2, a prompt registry, provenance views and an eval harness separately. No one has drawn the single data model linking stage → prompt_hash → attempt → decision → artifact → outcome. Without it, each is built with its own keys (llm_call_log has only content_piece_id and angle_gate_request_id typed). One root ADR should define 'AI provenance' before any of them is built.

CONSIDERING STRENGTHS THE LENSES MISSED. A4 Trust Ramp (graduated autonomy per tenant, admin_a4.py:13-44) and force-unpublish exist but are read-only and manual. They are the natural home for per-tenant AI autonomy levels (for example, auto-deliver vs hold-for-tenant-review) and should be extended rather than reinvented.
reprioritised_top10: 1. Gateway-written ledger v2, effort S-M (CIS migration owner). One row per attempt, including schema-fail and error attempts, with typed columns app, is_shadow, status, latency_ms, prompt_hash, attempt_no, subject_key and an experiment/test flag; judge repeats get separate rows; a failed log write alarms. Every other metric depends on this table telling the truth. Today it under-counts (client.py:139-145; call_log.py:155; lessons.md:13).

2. Data-class egress policy plus one read-only check. First, query llm_call_log for provider='openai' AND tenant_id IS NOT NULL to learn whether tenant content has already gone to the OpenAI API. Then add data_class to the catalog, skip disallowed route entries, redact PII, and write a tenant subprocessor list. This is the main live compliance and tenant-trust exposure (role_config.py:70,88-106; decide.py:192-239).

3. Hard spend and abuse limits now. Gateway budget checks per app × stage × tenant × day, API GW throttling plus a per-session cap and narration cache on TripPlanner, a narrate session-ownership check, and AWS Budgets and anomaly detection on acc1/acc3. Public Sonnet calls are unthrottled today (tripplanner.tf:435-445; handler.py:165-192).

4. One versioned gateway package (aa_llm) with a raw-call CI guard in all 3 repos, before Booking gets any Bedrock or llm_call_log grant. Retire the 269-line TripPlanner fork. Give each app its own ExternalId or RoleSessionName on acc3 so spend splits by app.

5. AI Use Register as code. For each stage: owner, decides vs assists, human gate, data class, golden set, budget scope, kill switch, review minutes per week. CI fails on unregistered stages or model_tier pins. Admin can pause any stage. This is the governance spine and holds evaluation ownership.

6. Route/prompt change management plus a committed per-stage eval suite. Golden sets and human labels move into the DB (AA-783). Judge stability (AA-801): median-of-3 always, every repeat logged, an A/A' noise band. A prompt-hash manifest is enforced in CI. A route change on a tenant- or customer-facing stage needs an eval run and a revert route, instead of going live in 20 s.

7. Source data quality gate and entity master. Score source completeness per raw tour before A1/A3 spend and route thin tours to human enrichment. Create one place/country ID shared by CIS, TripPlanner and Booking. Better AI output is capped by raw input (lessons.md:61; AA-690; lens-data.md:9).

8. Provenance and AI incident response. A generation manifest on every AI-produced artifact (stage, model, prompt_hash, job), bulk hold or unpublish by provenance, severity levels, a tenant notice template, and a runbook per alarm. Extend the A4 Trust Ramp into per-tenant autonomy levels.

9. Learning loop from outcomes. Capture tenant edit diffs and rejections (tenant_tour_versions.edit_source) and angle picks as labels. Add TripPlanner funnel analytics. Attribute inquiries and bookings back to tours, pieces, angles and keywords. Turn off Jev shadow questions and 100% shadows that have no calibration owner.

10. Cheap customer and Booking correctness before new AI features. Fix TripPlanner query embedding (input_type search_query, search.py:77) and add an active-tour filter to all recommendation reads. Add inquiry.submitted v1.2 (dates, pax, budget, language, message). Build deterministic Booking quote-integrity and margin guards and rate-upload anomaly diffs. Then start the assist-only inquiry triage brief as the first governed Booking AI feature.

syn.definition: For Adventure Asia, AI-first means AI does the reading, drafting, mapping and checking across the content supply (CIS A1–A3, T2–T10), the B2C front door (TripPlanner) and sales/ops (AA-Booking), while deterministic code owns every number (prices, margins, FX, dates, pax) and a named human or a deterministic check stands between any AI output and a customer, tenant, supplier or payment. It is not about adding more models. It is about making the AI that already decides things today (atoms, place cards, keyword purchases, T2/F9 gates, about 25 paid Jev questions) observable, budgeted, evaluated and switchable through one shared Model Gateway: a library plus the shared control plane in the acc2 RDS, owned by CIS. New AI goes only into blueprint phases whose data and contracts already exist. Pha 0/1 harden what runs now ('now'), Pha 2 adds one governed, draft-only Booking assistant ('next'), and Pha 3 scales customer-facing AI once there are funnel metrics and calibrated judges to measure it ('later').
principles: Numbers never come from a model. Prices, margins, FX, net rates, dates, pax and tax come only from deterministic engines or structured data (ADR 0005). Any number in AI text must match an allowed set, as in grounding.py:28-36, or the text fails closed.

AI drafts and checks; humans or deterministic rules release. No AI output reaches a customer, tenant, supplier or payment without a named human action or a deterministic gate. AI is never the checker in maker-checker.

One gateway, one ledger. Every LLM, Jev and embedding call in every repo goes through the CIS Model Gateway, packaged as a versioned library (not an HTTP service). The gateway itself, not the caller, writes one llm_call_log row per billed attempt, tagged by app.

Do not pay for inert AI. Every shadow model, Jev question and paid loop has an owner, an end date and a downstream action. Anything without them is switched off. Jev is about $11.8/week (lessons.md:13) on questions that are all shadow (migrations 182-196, 211).

No enforce without calibration. A judge or decision may gate content only after test-retest stability and human-label agreement are measured on a committed golden set (the Jev DB CHECK at 181_jev_decision_layer.sql:38-40, generalised). Until then, gates may trigger only a retry or an admin label.

Data class decides the vendor. Tenant content and customer PII go only to providers with a recorded DPA/ZDR (Bedrock acc3 yes; OpenAI platform API and TypeSafe only via allowlist). The gateway enforces this, not a convention.
Third-party text is data, never instructions. Supplier files, customer messages, SERP/PAA and tenant brand text feed schema-only stages with no state-changing tools, plus hard per-run spend caps.

Deterministic first, AI where it pays. Fix data quality, contracts and plain form fields before adding a model (blueprint Pha 1). Every AI feature must beat its no-AI alternative on a named business metric.

AI slots into blueprint phases and never competes with them. Pha 0/1 = governance and correctness of existing AI. Pha 2 = one draft-only Booking assistant after bk-002. Pha 3 = customer-facing AI expansion.
Review capacity is a budget. Each AI feature declares its reviewer-minutes per week and gets a queue-age alarm, because Nghiệp and chị Thư are the bottleneck (S234/10-agent-team-design.md:87).

guardrails: Numbers only from deterministic code. No LLM output may set, alter or restate a stored or sent price, margin, FX rate, net rate, tax, date or pax count. Any number in AI text must be in an allowed set (grounding.py:28-36), or the text fails closed. Tax is not shown until tax_rules exists (ADR 0005 decision 10).

A human or deterministic gate on every customer-, tenant-, supplier- or money-facing output. A named human sends, publishes, sets is_sent_to_customer, confirms bookings and verifies payments. AI is never counted as the maker-checker checker. Tenant-delivered T2/T9 gets a deterministic F9/B-class cut once Nghiệp approves, and the A4 force-unpublish net stays in place.

Writer-source-fidelity applies to all customer and tenant text. Background about a named place is allowed (A). Any unstated claim about the tour, such as activities, services, times, views or inclusions (B), is forbidden. Visa, health/altitude, safety and animal-welfare statements come only from curated Facts or structured data. The elephant-riding policy means human review, never strip or regenerate. No fabricated reviews or testimonials and no AI destination imagery.

Single gateway with a raw-call CI guard in CIS, TripPlanner and Booking that also covers scripts/. The gateway writes every billed attempt, including schema_fail and error. A failed log write raises an alarm and is treated as an incident. Ad-hoc LLM scripts use LLMClient with stage adhoc_<issue>.

Data-class egress is enforced in the gateway. Tenant content and customer PII go only to providers with a recorded DPA/ZDR. Passport, payment and full rooming data never go to a model. Deterministic PII redaction runs before egress. llm_shadow_log and quality_signal never hold raw customer PII and have a retention limit before Booking or TP customer text reaches the gateway.

Hard spend caps, with a stop and not only an alert, on every public endpoint and every batch job kind (ADR 0001 decision 4). Paid runs follow trial-3, then at most about 50 items. There are AWS Budgets and anomaly alerts on acc1, acc2 and acc3.

No enforce without calibration. Any judge, Jev question or score that gates content needs measured test-retest stability and ≥95% precision against human labels. Until then it may trigger only a retry or an admin label. Every shadow and paid question has an owner and an end date.

Change control for routes, prompts and rubrics. The prompt bytes hash is pinned in CI. A writer or judge change on a tenant- or customer-facing stage must attach a capped golden-set replay with an A/A' noise band and name a revert route. The 20-second live route edit stays audited and is reserved for rollback.

Third-party text is data. Extraction stages return a strict schema with no tools. Document text never chooses an action, recipient or price. Extracted values must be quoted verbatim from the source. Loops that spend money keep hard per-run caps. prompt_sanitize.py is self-injection containment only and is not a defence.

Kill switch and degraded mode. Every stage can be set to off or deterministic fallback from admin without a deploy. TripPlanner falls back to AA-authored day text, CIS jobs pause, and Booking works with zero AI. Writers are Anthropic-only on acc3, so an acc3 outage must degrade, not break customer flows.

Transparency. B2C narration (and any future chat) is labelled AI-assisted. Tenants receive a model-provider and subprocessor list. EU AI Act Art. 50 duties are checked with counsel before DE/FR/NL-facing AI launches.

Agent guardrails are fail-closed and tested. The hook parses argv and has a committed bypass table. No broad 'git push *' or 'terraform apply *' allowlists. Merges, deploys, Terraform apply and MCP writes stay with the orchestrator or Nghiệp. Never print or copy secrets.
metrics: Spend truth: monthly |External Spend estimate − Cost Explorer| per Bedrock account ≤5%. 100% of llm_call_log rows have app NOT NULL. *_log_write_failed = 0. Failed-attempt rows are present.
Inert spend: $/week on shadow-only Jev questions plus judge shadows without an end date, falling toward about $0 for anything without an owner.

Unit economics: AI $ per master tour published, per tenant piece delivered, per TripPlanner session (p95 and max) and per Booking inquiry, each reported beside a business outcome rather than in isolation.
Judge stability: T2 brand_fit test-retest range ≤1 point on a fixed 20-draft set (today 4–8). F9 verdict agreement ≥0.95 (today 0.87). Spearman(judge, human) ≥0.6.
Fabrication escape: F9 block / B-class sentences reaching tenants or B2C per 100 pieces (target 0). Place-card auto-check fact precision ≥95% on the human audit.
Data egress: 0 llm_call_log rows with a tenant_id or customer data on providers without a recorded DPA/ZDR.
Governance coverage: share of AI stages in the register that have an owner, golden set, budget scope and kill switch (target ≥80% by end of Pha 1). 0 model_tier pins. 0 calls on _GENERIC_FALLBACK.
Decision value: Jev questions in enforce with a calibration record, and grey-zone share per enforced question.
Business outcomes (needs funnel events first): inquiries per 1,000 TripPlanner sessions; consultant time from submitted_at to first reply; proposal_sent → confirmed rate.
Human load: reviewer-minutes per week per AI feature vs its declared budget; p90 queue age for A2 HITL, held pieces, place-card verify and the Booking inbox.
